mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW M135i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt N55B30 engine for the BMW M135i typically costs £4,000-£6,500 supply-only. A reconditioned unit is £3,200-£4,500, while a used engine is £1,800-£3,200. Supply & fit adds £600-£1,200 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of N55 engine failure in a BMW M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs include oil leaks (valve cover, oil filter housing, oil pan), long cranking times or rough idling (HPFP failure), and a rattling noise from the turbocharger at low speeds (wastegate rattle).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW M135i of relevant age (2012-2015) typically sits in the £5,000-£12,000 value band. A rebuilt N55B30 engine costs £4,000-£6,500, which is a significant but justifiable investment - especially when the alternative is selling a non-running car at a massive loss.

mainEntity.name: How long does a rebuilt BMW M135i engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A correctly rebuilt N55B30 engine using upgraded gaskets and components should last 100,000+ miles - often longer than the factory original. All engines supplied through EnginesMarket carry a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW M135i and BMW M140i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M135i uses the N55B30 3.0L turbocharged straight-six (320 hp), while the M140i uses the B58B30 3.0L turbocharged straight-six (340 hp). The B58 is a more modern engine with improved reliability and tuning potential, but the N55 remains a strong performer when properly maintained.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used BMW M135i engine from a breaker, or should I buy rebuilt?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used N55B30 engine is cheaper (£1,800-£3,200) but carries the same factory flaws that caused the original failure - oil leaks, HPFP issues, and wastegate rattle. A rebuilt engine costs more but eliminates those weaknesses with upgraded components.

commonProblems.h2: BMW M135i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW M135i's N55B30 turbocharged straight-six is a strong performer, but it has well-documented vulnerabilities. Oil leaks, HPFP failure, and wastegate rattle are the most common issues driving replacement demand. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded gaskets and components designed to address the original failure points - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: BMW M135i N55 Oil Leaks - Valve Cover, Oil Filter Housing & Oil Pan Gaskets
problems.rootCause: The N55 engine's gaskets degrade over time due to heat cycling, leading to oil leaks from the valve cover, oil filter housing, and oil pan.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the failed gasket (valve cover, oil filter housing, or oil pan)
repairOptions.longevity: Adds 50k-80k miles. Viable if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of all common leak points simultaneously
repairOptions.longevity: 80k+ mile lifespan. Cheaper long-term than doing one at a time

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with new gaskets, seals, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework, substituting the BMW M135i-appropriate value band from research: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. A typical BMW M135i of relevant age (2012-2015) sits in the £5,000-£12,000 band, so a rebuilt engine is generally viable.
problems.recommendation: If you catch oil leaks early, a gasket replacement is cost-effective. However, if the engine has been driven with low oil pressure or the leaks have been ignored for extended periods, debris may have contaminated the bottom end - in which case a full rebuilt unit with upgraded gaskets is the safer long-term investment.

problems.group: BMW M135i N55 High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure
problems.h4: BMW M135i N55 High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure
problems.rootCause: The HPFP is a critical component in the direct fuel injection system. It can fail, leading to long cranking times, loss of power, rough idling, and engine stalling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the faulty HPFP with a new OEM or upgraded unit
repairOptions.longevity: 80k+ mile lifespan. Viable if caught before other damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with new HPFP, injectors, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP failure caused fuel contamination or internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A BMW M135i of relevant age typically sits in the £5,000-£12,000 band. HPFP replacement is well within value.
problems.recommendation: HPFP failure is serious but repairable without full engine replacement if caught when the first symptom appears (long cranking, rough idle). A specialist HPFP replacement costs £500-£1,000. However, if the car has been driven with a failing HPFP for an extended period, fuel contamination may have damaged the injectors and cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt engine is the safer option.
